newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia sells HRK80 mln 91-day T-bills, rate falls.
newsitem.headline: Croatia sells HRK80 mln 91-day T-bills, rate falls.

text.p: Croatia's Finance Ministry said it raised 80 million kuna in 91-day treasury bills at a primary auction on Tuesday.
The issued volume overshot the target by 20 million kuna after bids totalled almost 115 million, it said in a statement.
The price rose to 97.532 percent from 97.461 two weeks ago, with the rate falling 30 basis points to 10.15 percent.
Banks were said to have bought 87.375 percent of the issue. Bills are payable in two days and they mature on September 25.
Full auction details are available on page MFHT.
The ministry set the new auction for July 8, when it will offer 150 million kuna worth of 42-day T-bills. They were last issued at a 9.26-percent interest late in May.
Foreign investors have no direct access to T-bill auctions but can place their bids through Croatian banks. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
